A person is viewed as men tally sound if he or she does not suf fer from anxiety, depression, or other forms of psychological symp tomatology. This prevailing formula tion never gets to the heart of Well ness; to do so, we must define mental health as the presence of the positive. To explicate the positive is, how ever, to grapple with basic values and ideals of the human experience. These values are no less evident in definitions of human suffering, al though consensus in identification of the negative is somehow easier to achieve. Despite these challenges, much has been written, within the field of psychology and outside it, regarding the contours of positive psychological functioning. DEFINING FEATURES OF WELL-BEING

claims.text: Research on psychological problems significantly dwarfs literature focused on positive psychological functioning.
Prevailing formulations equate mental health with the absence of illness or psychological symptomatology.
Defining mental health effectively requires conceptualizing it as the presence of positive psychological functioning rather than merely the absence of illness.
Consensus on defining negative psychological states is easier to achieve than consensus on defining positive psychological functioning.

limitations.text: Prior psychological literature equates health with the absence of illness rather than exploring positive wellness.
Explicating positive psychological functioning requires grappling with basic values and ideals, making consensus difficult to achieve.
